text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former conservative prime minister Carl Bildt says he does not rule out Nato membership for Sweden.
- Support for the ruling Social Democrat Party has fallen to 34 percent from 35.5 percent while support for the conservative Moderates has risen to 28 percent from 24.5 percent, a poll shows.
Meanwhile, support for the Left Party is steady at 11.5 percent since the last poll despite an admission by Left Party leader Gudrun Schyman that she had a drinking problem.
- Mortgage rates are at an all-time low.
- Telecoms operator Telia lost the first round first round of a courtroom battle surrounding whether it should allow phone sex providers to use its telephone lines.
- Sweden had the highest taxes in the European Union in 1995, statistics show.
- Finance Minister Erik Asbrink decline comment about whether he has been in contact with Swedish commercial banks Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken about a possible merger.

- Swedish and British financial authorities are looking into fluctuations in the share price of Sintercast, a large stake of which was found to be held by Morgan Grenfell funds now under investigation.
- Swedish businessman Adolf Lundin is to invest 100 million crowns in a hunt for oil in Tanzania.
